name: Diltiazem
summary: A non-dihydropyridine calcium channel blocker that slows AV nodal conduction, making it a mainstay for rate control in atrial fibrillation and for angina and hypertension.
mechanism: Blocks L-type calcium channels in cardiac tissue and vascular smooth muscle, depressing SA/AV nodal automaticity and conduction while dilating arterioles.

dosing.adult: Hypertension/angina: extended-release 120–240 mg once daily; atrial fibrillation rate control: IV bolus 0.25 mg/kg then infusion, or oral ER 120–360 mg/day

contraindications: Heart failure with reduced ejection fraction
warnings: Avoid IV combination with beta blockers (stacked bradycardia/conduction block)
CYP3A4 inhibition raises levels of simvastatin, cyclosporine, and others
Bradycardia and AV block, especially in elderly
safety.overdose: Bradycardia, AV block, hypotension; treat with calcium gluconate, atropine, and supportive care.

clinicalPearls: Vascular-selective relative to verapamil but still negatively inotropic — the reflex is to avoid it in HFrEF.
Its CYP3A4 inhibition matters clinically: limit simvastatin doses and monitor cyclosporine when co-prescribed.
good: AF rate control and angina in patients with preserved ejection fraction.
bad: HFrEF, high-grade AV block, or combination with IV beta blockers.
